text:
alex: Heads-up — after OFED upgrade (5.6 -> 5.8) rolled to a slice of eu-central GPU pool we are seeing intermittent NCCL transport fallbacks to TCP and ~25-35% allreduce throughput drop on 8xA100 instances. dmesg shows mlx5 timeouts.
pat: Which node types and driver stack exactly?
sana: Any error excerpts / logs? short thread so we can triage quickly.
alex: Node flavor: gpu.p8.0 (8xA100 80GB). NVIDIA driver: 535.86.10, CUDA 12.2, kernel 6.1. Logs snippet:
```
[ 1234.567890] mlx5 0000:81:00.0: mlx5_core: FW error recovery triggered
[ 1234.568210] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: CQE completion timeout on QP 0x1f4
[ 1234.568411] ucma: causing errno 110
```
nccl error on one job:
```
NCCL WARN Call to ibv_create_cq failed: Input/output error
NCCL INFO Rank 3 -> Rank 5 transport fallback to TCP
NCCL ERROR Allreduce timed out after 120000 ms
```
pat: Oof. Are fallbacks happening for the same ranks/nodes each time or random?
alex: Mostly the same subset (~6/40 nodes) in the canary pool. If we detach a node from the pool and reattach after firmware reflash some recover, others keep flapping.
mike: Did we change any kernel params or mlx5 modules during the OFED update? Could be a doorbell related regression.
alex: OFED upgrade pulled in mlx5_core 5.8.x binary + new fw package. No explicit kernel param changes in our rollout. We applied default vendor configs.
sana: Quick mitigation idea: force NCCL to avoid IB/RC/DC transport on affected runs to prevent hangs. Env to try: `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` or force sockets: `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0` (not great perf but stable). Anyone tried this in prod?
pat: We have a job with NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on stage; throughput drop ~40% but completes reliably. That aligns with expected TCP vs IB perf.
alex: Workarounds we tested:
- downgrade OFED on one node -> IB restores, nccl back to IB and throughput good
- NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 -> job completes on all nodes but with higher cost
- pinning to older driver (534.x) with same OFED sometimes helps but not stable

So two paths: rollback OFED for affected nodes or enforce TCP fallback until vendor fixes.
oncall-bot: incident created: INFRA-2026-47 — "eu-central OFED5.8 -> NCCL transport regressions" assigned to alex, severity: medium, link: https://tracker.redwood/INFRA-2026-47
mike: Rolling back OFED cluster-wide will be heavy; can we target only that canary slice and nodes showing CQ timeouts?
alex: Plan proposal:
1) Quarantine affected nodes from production pools (move to remediation pool) — pat
2) Reflash firmware and re-run quick nccl microbench -> if green, return to pool — alex
3) If reflashing doesn't stick, rollback OFED package to 5.6 on those nodes or pin driver version — sana
4) For in-flight/urgent customer jobs, set `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` via job wrapper until resolved — mike

pat: I'll start quarantine action now and add node list to the incident ticket.
sana: Engaging vendor support (Mellanox) — I've attached dmesg and nccl logs to the ticket.
deploy-bot: deploy-log: OFED 5.8 rollout started for eu-central-gpu-canary at 2026-03-16T09:12:04Z by deploy/infra-rollout
alex: Cost note: if we force TCP for long-running jobs, expect 30-50% longer runtimes and corresponding spot cost bump. We should notify SRE and customers if we need to extend.
mike: Also we should add a kernel/dmesg metric to alert on mlx5 CQE timeouts so we catch regressions earlier.
alex: Agree. Action owners: pat(quarantine), alex(reflash+test), sana(vendor), mike(alerting+job-wrapper). We'll update ticket INFRA-2026-47 with progress. :thumbsup:
pat: Quarantine done for 6 nodes — moved to remediation pool, added tag `ofed-5.8-flap`. Will wait for alex tests.
